#Set up the vectors
```{r}
#The outcome vector X:
X <- t(counts_batch_corrected_combined) #MINT expects samples as rows and genes as columns, so the data must be transposed


#The outcome vector Y:
outcome <- filtered_meta_combined$status #status is affected or unaffected

#Defining where the data comes from:
study <- filtered_meta_combined$data #data is RRC or Mote_CIL. !!!!!!!!!!!!!!Real_timepoint.x also comes into play here

#Experiemental Design
table(outcome,study)
```

#Plot the data table(outcome,study) to see sample divisions
```{r}
# Create a data frame from the table
df <- as.data.frame(table(outcome, study))
colnames(df) <- c("Outcome", "Study", "Count")  # rename columns for ggplot

# Grouped bar plot
ggplot(data = df, aes(x = Outcome, y = Count, fill = Study)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") + #bar plot
  geom_text(aes(label = Count), #creates the labels near the bar
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
            vjust = -0.3) +
  labs(
    title = "Sample Distribution by Outcome and Study",
    x = "Outcome",
    y = "Number of Samples",
    fill = "Study"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Mote_CIL" = "#576CB9", "RRC" = "#48A948"))

```

#Preliminary PCA
##Determine number of components
```{r}
pca_combined <- pca(X, ncomp = 10, center = TRUE, scale = TRUE)
plot(pca_combined)
```


##Visualize sample groupings
```{r}
plotIndiv(pca_combined, group = outcome, ind.names = FALSE,
          legend = TRUE, title = 'PCA of Combined Data, comp 1-2')
```
The samples group by study with 32% explained variance. 




#MINT sPLS-DA Model
#Stratify the data into training, validation, and test data. This will identify which samples go into which group. !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
```{r}
set.seed(123) #A starting number used in the random generator. It controls the random number sequence used to select samples and keeps it consistent for reproducability.

#Create strat_matrix using both outcome and study
strat_matrix <- interaction(outcome, study, drop = TRUE)

#Reserve 65% of the strat_matrix for training
train_strat <- createDataPartition(strat_matrix,
  p = 0.65, #65% of the data
  list = FALSE) #returns a matrix instead of a list

#Clearly separate the remaining 20% of the data for testing.
test_strat <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(X)), train_strat) #takes the samples from 1-113 defined as training and removes them. the remainders are the test set.
```


##Create separate datasets using the stratified data so that I can train, validate, and test the model.
```{r}
#Training data
X_train <- X[train_strat,] #the gene counts
outcome_train <- outcome[train_strat] #the status of the samples after exposure
study_train <- study[train_strat] #the sample origin


#Test data
X_test <- X[test_strat,] #the gene counts
outcome_test <- outcome[test_strat] #the status of the samples after exposure
study_test <- study[test_strat] #the sample origin
```


##Confirm sample distriutions and sample numbers 
```{r}
#Training
table(outcome_train, study_train)
nrow(X_train)

#Test
table(outcome_test, study_test)
nrow(X_test)
```

##Tune the model using only the training data
```{r}
#grid of possible keepX values. This specifies the number of genes the model will test retaining on each component. Start at 1 gene, end at 100 genes, increase by 1 each time

#mahalanobis.dist
tune_mint_splsda1 <- tune(X=X_train, Y=outcome_train, study=study_train,
                             ncomp=10,
                             validation = 'loo',
                             measure = 'BER',
                             dist = "mahalanobis.dist",
                             test.keepX = seq(1,100,1), #From Natalia? Comment above.
                             method = "mint.splsda")
plot(tune_mint_splsda1, sd=FALSE) #sd = false due to LOO CV


#centroids.dist
tune_mint_splsda2 <- tune(X=X_train, Y=outcome_train, study=study_train,
                             ncomp=10,
                             validation = 'loo',
                             measure = 'BER',
                             dist = "centroids.dist",
                             test.keepX = seq(1,100,1), #From Natalia. Comment above.
                             method = "mint.splsda")
plot(tune_mint_splsda2, sd=FALSE) #sd = false due to LOO CV


#max.dist
tune_mint_splsda3 <- tune(X=X_train, Y=outcome_train, study=study_train,
                             ncomp=10,
                             validation = 'loo',
                             measure = 'BER',
                             dist = "max.dist",
                             test.keepX = seq(1,100,1), #From Natalia. Comment above.
                             method = "mint.splsda")
plot(tune_mint_splsda3, sd=FALSE) #sd = false due to LOO CV
```
The example pipeline doesn't pre-test a dist to use in the tuning model. I realized I might need to specify a different distance while following a splsda pipeline. After looking at these three distance plots, the one with the lowest BER is mahalanobis with 8 components.

```{r}
#sPLS-DA model
mint_splsda_tune <- mint.splsda(X=X_tune, Y=outcome_tune, study=study_tune, ncomp = 2)

mint_splsda_perf_tune <- perf(mint_splsda, folds = 2, nrepeat =50)
plot(mint_splsda_perf)
```




##Extract the optimal keepX parameter
```{r}
optimal_ncomp <- 8

optimal_keepX <-tune_mint_splsda1$choice.keepX[1:optimal_ncomp]
optimal_keepX
```
ncomp is the number of components to include in the model. optimal_keepx is determining the the optimal amount of features for each component

#Train MINT sPLS-DA model with the tuned data
```{r}
#sPLS-DA model
mint_splsda <- mint.splsda(X=X_train, Y=outcome_train, study=study_train, ncomp=optimal_ncomp, keepX = optimal_keepX)


#Plots
plotIndiv(mint_splsda, study='global', legend = TRUE,
          title = 'MINT sPLS-DA',
          subtitle = 'Global', ellipse = TRUE)

plotIndiv(mint_splsda, study='all.partial', legend = TRUE,
          title = 'MINT sPLS-DA',
          subtitle = paste('all.partial', 1:2))
```

#Test MINT sPLS-DA model with the tuned data
##Determine which distance metric to use
```{r}
mint_splsda_perf <- perf(mint_splsda, folds = 2, nrepeat =50)
plot(mint_splsda_perf)
```


##predict outcome of samples
```{r}
mint_splsda_pred <- predict(mint_splsda, newdata = X_test, dist = "max.dist", study.test = study_test)
```



#Determine study success
```{r}
#Create a matrix of predicted classifications to determine sensitivity and accuracy
mint_results <- data.frame(
  Actual = outcome_test, #affected or unaffected
  Predicted = mint_splsda_pred$class$max.dist[,1], #results of the prediction above
  study = study_test) #the sample origin (lab and field)

#Calculate global performance
global_perf <- confusionMatrix(
  as.factor(mint_results$Predicted),
  as.factor(mint_results$Actual),
  positive = "affected")
global_perf

#Calculate the performance by each study
##field
field_perf<- subset(mint_results, study == "RRC") #remember, study includes lab and field data. must be subset.
field_cm <- confusionMatrix(
  as.factor(field_perf$Predicted),
  as.factor(field_perf$Actual),
  positive = "affected")
field_cm

##lab
lab_perf<- subset(mint_results, study == "Mote_CIL") #remember, study includes lab and field data. must be subset
lab_cm <- confusionMatrix(
  as.factor(lab_perf$Predicted),
  as.factor(lab_perf$Actual),
  positive = "affected")
lab_cm
```

###Plot the Confusion Matrices
```{r}
#ggplot needs the input to be a data frame, so turn the matrices into df
global_df <- as.data.frame(global_perf$table)
field_df <- as.data.frame(field_cm$table)
lab_df <- as.data.frame(lab_cm$table)

#Global
ggplot(data = global_df, aes(x = Reference, y = Prediction, fill = Freq))+
  geom_tile() + #This is what creates confusion plots in ggplot
  geom_text(aes(label = Freq), size = 10) + #This is what labels the tiles
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "paleturquoise", high = "cyan4")+ 
  labs(
    title = "Global Test Confusion Matrix",
    x = "Predicted",
    y = "Actual",
    fill = "Count")

#Field
ggplot(data = field_df, aes(x = Reference, y = Prediction, fill = Freq))+
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = Freq), size = 10) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "palegreen1", high = "forestgreen")+
  labs(
    title = "Field Test Confusion Matrix",
    x = "Predicted",
    y = "Actual",
    fill = "Count")

#lab
ggplot(data = lab_df, aes(x = Reference, y = Prediction, fill = Freq))+
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = Freq), size = 10) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "lightblue1", high = "steelblue")+
  labs(
    title = "Lab Test Confusion Matrix",
    x = "Predicted",
    y = "Actual",
    fill = "Count")
```



##AUC Plots
```{r}
#Get test prediction scores from my 8 components. (test_pred_scores will be a subset of mint_splsda_pred that only contains info on the first 8 components.)
test_pred_scores <- mint_splsda_pred$predict[,"affected",8]

#Create a data frame with the predicted probabilities for roc analysis
roc_data <- data.frame (outcome = as.integer(outcome_test == "affected"), test_pred_scores, study_test)

#Global
roc_global <- ggplot(roc_data, aes(d = outcome, m = test_pred_scores)) + geom_roc(color = "cyan3", n.cuts = 0) + #n.cuts removes extra data labels
  labs(
    title = "Global AUROC Curve",
    x = "False Positive Rate",
    y = "True Positive Rate")
roc_global

#Field
roc_field <- ggplot(roc_data[roc_data$study_test == "RRC",], aes(d = outcome, m = test_pred_scores)) + geom_roc(color = "green3", n.cuts = 0) + 
  labs(
    title = "Field AUROC Curve",
    x = "False Positive Rate",
    y = "True Positive Rate")
roc_field
  

#Lab
roc_lab <- ggplot(roc_data[roc_data$study_test == "Mote_CIL",], aes(d = outcome, m = test_pred_scores)) + geom_roc(color = "steelblue2", n.cuts = 0) + 
  labs(
    title = "Lab AUROC Curve",
    x = "False Positive Rate",
    y = "True Positive Rate")
roc_lab
```
